name: Greek Pork Chops with Zucchini, Tomatoes and Feta

fit.reason: 482 cal is inside 400-650; 9g carbs is well under the 35g cap; no seafood; skillet sear-then-braise scales to 14 by weigh-and-divide; budget meal-prep dinner.

duplicate_check.evidence: Not a duplicate. Closest catalog Greek/pork entry is greek-pork-souvlaki-rice-bowls, but that is marinated grilled pork tenderloin over rice (different cut, method, and starch) rather than seared bone-in chops braised with zucchini, tomatoes, olives and feta. The catalog's ~15 pork-chop dishes are all creamy/cheesy/gravy/rice/potato builds (creamy-mushroom-pork-chops, marry-me-pork-chops, southern-smothered, no-peek-rice, cheesy-hash-brown, etc.) with none carrying the Greek zucchini-tomato-feta-olive profile. accepted-slugs pork entries (creamy-garlic-herb-wine-pork-chops, thai-coconut-curry-pork-shoulder) are unrelated flavor families.

cross_protein_collision: Structurally this is a Greek/Mediterranean protein-over-non-starchy-veg skillet finished with feta, cherry tomatoes, olives and oregano. The decider should watch other proteins' pools for the same dish built on chicken or turkey (e.g. a 'Greek chicken skillet with zucchini, tomatoes and feta' or a baked-feta chicken), which would be the same dinner with the protein swapped.
cuisine_note: Greek / Mediterranean widens a catalog that skews American/Tex-Mex; distinct angle from all existing creamy/cheese pork-chop pan-sauces.
